I read the whole file. I did not open any related source files, and I did not run or compile any replacement. The only repetition is dual: kernel against cokernel, and cycles against opcycles.

The closest candidates were:
- tateOpcyclesIsoNegOne_naturality and tateCyclesIsoZero_naturality. Each is a cancel-epi or cancel-mono argument that unfolds a Rep functor and then applies a different chains or cochains lemma. The unfolding steps differ.
- The two NatIso.ofComponents calc blocks (tateCohomologyNegOneNatIsoKernelNorm and tateCohomologyZeroNatIsoCokernelNorm). Both are long associativity-and-rewrite chains for a mono and an epi respectively. A shared lemma would have to be stated twice, once with a mono and once with an epi. Each statement would also need its own naturality hypotheses (normSequence_first_naturality and normKernelFunctor_map_ι on one side, normSequence_last_naturality and normCokernelFunctor_π_map on the other). That is not a shared proof.

The calc blocks could be shortened with simp, rw or reassoc lemmas. That is routine proof golf, not reuse of nontrivial mathematical reasoning, so I did not report it.
